documents.title: Guidance on Nonclinical Safety Studies for the Conduct of Human Clinical Trials and Marketing Authorization for Pharmaceuticals

sections.title: High Dose Selection for General Toxicity Studies
ESTIMATION OF THE FIRST DOSE IN HUMAN
Single-Dose Trials at Sub-therapeutic Doses or into the Anticipated Therapeutic Range

source_units.source_text: The purpose of this document is to recommend international standards for, and promote harmonisation of, the nonclinical safety studies recommended to support human clinical trials of a given scope and duration as well as marketing authorization for pharmaceuticals. Harmonisation of the guidance for nonclinical safety studies will help to define the current recommendations and reduce the likelihood that substantial differences will exist among regions. This guidance should facilitate the timely conduct of clinical trials, reduce the use of animals in accordance with the 3R (reduce/refine/replace) principles and reduce the use of other drug development resources.

trace.extraction_method: automated text extraction with manual verification

source_units.source_text: The development of a pharmaceutical is a stepwise process involving an evaluation of both animal and human safety information. The goals of the nonclinical safety evaluation generally include a characterisation of toxic effects with respect to target organs, dose dependence, relationship to exposure, and, when appropriate, potential reversibility. This information is used to estimate an initial safe starting dose and dose range for the human trials and to identify parameters for clinical monitoring for potential adverse effects.

trace.extraction_method: automated text extraction with manual verification

source_units.source_text: This guideline applies to the situations usually encountered during the development of pharmaceuticals and should be viewed as providing general guidance for drug development. For biotechnology-derived products, refer to ICH Guideline S6. Biotechnology-derived products can refer to this M3(R2) guideline for issues not covered in ICH S6. Pharmaceuticals under development for indications in life-threatening or serious diseases (e.g., advanced cancer, resistant HIV infection) without current effective therapy also warrant a case-by-case approach. Nonclinical safety studies for anticancer pharmaceuticals are specifically outlined in ICH S9.

trace.extraction_method: automated text extraction with manual verification

source_units.source_text: The nonclinical safety studies should be conducted in compliance with Good Laboratory Practice (GLP). The nonclinical safety studies should be designed and performed with high scientific standard and conduct. Consideration should be given to the 3R principles to reduce the number of animals used.

trace.extraction_method: automated text extraction with manual verification

source_units.source_text: In general toxicity studies, the high dose should be selected based on one of the following endpoints: (1) Maximum Tolerated Dose (MTD), (2) Saturating exposure, (3) Maximum Feasible Dose (MFD), (4) Limit dose of 1000 mg/kg/day, or (5) 50-fold exposure margin relative to clinical exposure. A dose of 1000 mg/kg/day is generally considered the maximum limit dose for general toxicity studies. However, if 1000 mg/kg/day does not result in a 10-fold exposure margin and the clinical dose exceeds 1 g/day, testing up to 2000 mg/kg/day or the MFD should be considered.

trace.extraction_method: automated text extraction with manual verification

source_units.source_text: Doses providing a 50-fold margin of exposure (group mean AUC of parent drug or active metabolite) to the clinical exposure are generally considered an acceptable endpoint for high dose selection in general toxicity studies in rodents and non-rodents for pharmaceuticals with low toxicity potential.

trace.extraction_method: automated text extraction with manual verification

source_units.source_text: The core battery of safety pharmacology studies includes the assessment of vital organ functions on cardiovascular, central nervous (CNS) and respiratory systems, and should generally be conducted before human exposure, in accordance with ICH S7A and S7B. Supplemental and follow-up safety pharmacology studies (e.g., renal, gastrointestinal) can be conducted during later clinical development when warranted. Secondary pharmacodynamics (off-target effects) should also be evaluated.

trace.extraction_method: automated text extraction with manual verification

source_units.source_text: In vitro metabolic and plasma protein binding data for animals and humans and systemic exposure data in species used for repeated-dose toxicity studies (ICH S3A) should be evaluated before initiating clinical trials. Further information on absorption, distribution, metabolism and excretion (ADME) in animals should be generated during clinical development.

trace.extraction_method: automated text extraction with manual verification

source_units.source_text: Data on acute toxicity can be obtained from appropriately conducted dose escalation or range-finding studies and can support single dose clinical trials in humans. Non-lethal acute toxicity studies should be conducted rather than classic LD50 testing. Acute toxicity data are also useful to predict the consequences of human overdose situations and should be available to support Phase III.

trace.extraction_method: automated text extraction with manual verification

source_units.source_text: The recommended duration of repeated-dose toxicity studies to support clinical trials depends on the intended duration of the clinical trial. For a single dose clinical trial, minimum repeated-dose toxicity study duration is 2 weeks in rodents and 2 weeks in non-rodents. For clinical trials up to 2 weeks, repeated-dose toxicity duration is 2 weeks in rodents and non-rodents. For clinical trials up to 1 month, toxicity study duration is 1 month in rodents and non-rodents. For clinical trials up to 3 months, toxicity duration is 3 months in rodents and non-rodents. For clinical trials up to 6 months, toxicity duration is 6 months in rodents and non-rodents. For clinical trials exceeding 6 months, 6 months in rodents and 9 months in non-rodents are recommended (Table 1).

trace.extraction_method: automated text extraction with manual verification

source_units.source_text: To support marketing authorization (MA), repeated-dose toxicity studies of 6 months duration in rodents and 9 months duration in non-rodents are recommended for pharmaceuticals intended for clinical administration longer than 3 months or for chronic use (Table 2). For clinical indications up to 2 weeks, 1 month rodent and non-rodent studies are recommended. For indications up to 1 month, 3 months studies are recommended.

trace.extraction_method: automated text extraction with manual verification

source_units.source_text: The estimation of the first dose in humans is an important element to safeguard subjects participating in first-in-human studies. All of the relevant nonclinical data, including the pharmacological dose response, the pharmacological/toxicological profile, and pharmacokinetics, should be considered when determining the recommended starting dose in humans. In general, the No Observed Adverse Effect Level (NOAEL) determined in the most relevant animal species, combined with appropriate safety factors, is used to estimate the initial clinical dose. When biologically active pharmaceuticals have potent agonistic effects or high species specificity, MABEL or other pharmacologically based approaches should be considered.

trace.extraction_method: automated text extraction with manual verification

source_units.source_text: Exploratory clinical trials can be conducted early in human drug development under specific approaches (Approaches 1 through 5) before standard full repeated-dose toxicity testing. These approaches involve limited human exposure, have no therapeutic intent, and are used to investigate PK, PD, receptor occupancy, or target selection.

trace.extraction_method: automated text extraction with manual verification

source_units.source_text: Approach 1 (Microdose Approach 1) involves administering a total dose of not more than 100 µg (as a single dose or divided doses) that is also not more than 1/100th of the NOAEL and not more than 1/100th of the pharmacologically active dose. Approach 1 is supported by an extended single-dose toxicity study in one mammalian species (usually rodent) with 14-day observation.

trace.extraction_method: automated text extraction with manual verification

source_units.source_text: Approach 2 (Microdose Approach 2) involves up to 5 administrations of not more than 100 µg per administration (total accumulated dose not more than 500 µg), with each dose not exceeding 1/100th of the NOAEL. Approach 2 can be used for PET receptor occupancy studies and is supported by a 7-day or 14-day toxicity study in a single mammalian species.

trace.extraction_method: automated text extraction with manual verification

source_units.source_text: Approach 3 involves single-dose trials at sub-therapeutic doses or into the anticipated therapeutic range. The clinical starting dose should be based on safety factors from animal NOAELs. Approach 3 is supported by a 2-week repeated-dose toxicity study in a rodent and a 2-week repeated-dose toxicity study in a non-rodent.

trace.extraction_method: automated text extraction with manual verification

source_units.source_text: Approach 4 involves multiple dose clinical trials of up to 14 days duration into the therapeutic range. Approach 4 is supported by 2-week repeated-dose toxicity studies in both a rodent and a non-rodent species. Approach 5 involves multiple dose clinical trials of up to 14 days duration supported by a 2-week rodent toxicity study and a non-rodent confirmatory study showing that the rodent NOAEL is non-toxic in the non-rodent.

trace.extraction_method: automated text extraction with manual verification

source_units.source_text: It is preferable to evaluate local tolerance by the intended therapeutic route as part of the general toxicity studies; stand alone studies are generally not recommended. To support limited human administration by non-therapeutic routes (e.g., a single i.v. dose to determine absolute bioavailability of an oral drug), a single dose local tolerance study in a single species is considered appropriate.

trace.extraction_method: automated text extraction with manual verification

source_units.source_text: Prior to first-in-human clinical trials, an assay for gene mutation (Ames test) and an in vitro mammalian cell assay or an in vivo test for chromosomal damage should be completed. A complete battery of tests for genotoxicity (Option 1 or Option 2 in ICH S2) should be completed before the initiation of Phase II clinical trials.

trace.extraction_method: automated text extraction with manual verification

source_units.source_text: Carcinogenicity studies are recommended for pharmaceuticals whose expected clinical use is continuous for at least 6 months, or is frequently intermittent for chronic or recurrent conditions. Carcinogenicity studies should be completed and submitted with the marketing authorization application (MAA/NDA), unless clinical safety concerns warrant earlier conduct before Phase III or Phase II.

trace.extraction_method: automated text extraction with manual verification

source_units.source_text: Men can be included in Phase I and II trials before the conduct of the male fertility study since an evaluation of the male reproductive organs is performed in the repeated-dose toxicity studies. A male fertility study (ICH S5) should be completed before the initiation of large scale or long duration clinical trials (e.g., Phase III trials).

trace.extraction_method: automated text extraction with manual verification

source_units.source_text: Women not of childbearing potential (i.e., permanently sterilised, postmenopausal) can be included in clinical trials without reproduction toxicity studies if the relevant repeated-dose toxicity studies (which include an evaluation of the female reproductive organs) have been conducted. Postmenopausal is defined as 12 months with no menses without an alternative medical cause.

trace.extraction_method: automated text extraction with manual verification

source_units.source_text: Women of childbearing potential (WOCBP) can be included in early clinical trials when precautions to prevent pregnancy are used. Precautions include pregnancy testing and use of highly effective contraceptive methods. Preliminary embryofetal developmental toxicity studies in two species can support the inclusion of up to 150 WOCBP receiving investigational treatment for up to 3 months before definitive reprotox testing. Definitive embryo-fetal development studies in two species must be completed prior to the inclusion of WOCBP in Phase III or extensive clinical trials.

trace.extraction_method: automated text extraction with manual verification

source_units.source_text: Before pregnant women are included in clinical trials, female reproduction toxicity studies (fertility, embryo-fetal development, and pre- and post-natal development) in two species and the standard battery of genotoxicity studies should be completed, and safety data from previous human exposure should be available.

trace.extraction_method: automated text extraction with manual verification

source_units.source_text: When pediatric populations are to be included in clinical trials, safety data from previous adult animal and human exposure should be evaluated. The conduct of any juvenile animal toxicity studies should be considered only when previous animal data and human safety data are judged to be insufficient. If a juvenile study is warranted, one relevant species, preferably rodent, is generally considered adequate.

trace.extraction_method: automated text extraction with manual verification

source_units.source_text: All new pharmaceuticals should be evaluated for the potential to produce immunotoxicity using standard repeated-dose toxicity studies (hematology, lymphoid organ weights, and histology). If signs of immunotoxic potential are observed, additional immunotoxicity studies (in accordance with ICH S8) should be conducted before Phase III or earlier.

trace.extraction_method: automated text extraction with manual verification

source_units.source_text: An initial assessment of phototoxicity potential based on photochemical properties (UV/Vis light absorption between 290 and 700 nm with molar extinction coefficient > 1000 M-1 cm-1) should be performed. If phototoxic potential is identified and the drug distributes to skin or eye, experimental testing (in vitro 3T3 NRU phototoxicity assay, in vivo, or clinical phototoxicity testing) should be completed prior to Phase III.

trace.extraction_method: automated text extraction with manual verification

source_units.source_text: For pharmaceuticals that produce central nervous system (CNS) effects, nonclinical abuse liability studies should support Phase III clinical trials. The evaluation includes receptor binding profiles, behavioral pharmacology (drug discrimination and self-administration), and physical dependence assessments.

trace.extraction_method: automated text extraction with manual verification

source_units.source_text: Nonclinical qualification of impurities and degradants should be conducted in accordance with ICH Q3A and Q3B. For human drug metabolites, nonclinical safety qualification (MIST) is warranted when a metabolite is formed at > 10% of total drug-related exposure in humans and at significantly lower exposure in toxicity animal species.

trace.extraction_method: automated text extraction with manual verification

source_units.source_text: For combination drug development, combination toxicity studies of duration equivalent to the clinical trial up to a maximum duration of 90 days are recommended. A 90-day combination toxicity study in a single relevant species supports marketing authorization. If both individual entities are well characterized and no pharmacokinetic or toxicological interaction is anticipated, nonclinical combination studies might not be warranted.

trace.extraction_method: automated text extraction with manual verification

source_units.source_text: Continuing efforts are underway among ICH regions to further harmonize nonclinical safety requirements and reduce unnecessary animal use while maintaining high safety standards for human clinical trials.

trace.extraction_method: automated text extraction with manual verification

source_units.source_text: Endnotes define specific quantitative parameters: Note 1 defines the 50-fold exposure margin based on group mean AUC; Note 2 defines male reproductive evaluation in repeated-dose toxicity; Note 3 defines highly effective contraception requirements; Note 4 defines preliminary embryo-fetal studies with a minimum of 6 dams per group; Note 5 details pregnancy risk baseline rates.

trace.extraction_method: automated text extraction with manual verification
